key_insight: SCOPE leverages the fact that novel classes often appear as unlabeled background in base-training 3D scenes to enrich class prototypes, enabling reliable few-shot learning without catastrophic forgetting. This scene-contextualized prototype enrichment produces more discriminative representations from sparse annotations.
problem_solved: Incremental Few-Shot 3D segmentation suffers from catastrophic forgetting and poor prototype quality when only a few annotations are available; existing methods also ignore informative unlabeled regions in base scenes that could help learn novel classes.
method: Scene-context mining: identify and aggregate unlabeled background regions in base-training point clouds that likely contain novel-category samples.
Prototype enrichment: build context-aware, discriminative prototypes by pooling scene-level features and few-shot exemplars to amplify weak supervision.

Incremental learning with prototype regularization: integrate enriched prototypes into the segmentation model (plug-and-play) and use prototype alignment/distillation to avoid forgetting of base classes.
impact: SCOPE makes incremental few-shot 3D segmentation more practical by improving novel-class learning from sparse labels while preserving past knowledge, reducing annotation burden for 3D applications like robotics and AR. Practitioners can plug SCOPE into existing pipelines to boost performance on point-cloud segmentation tasks with minimal extra data.
